newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea intervenes to support won - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea intervenes to support won - dealers.

text.p: South Korea's central Bank of Korea (BOK) stepped in the foreign exchange market in Friday's mid-morning trading to boost the won against the dollar, dealers said.
They said the BOK began to sell dollars at the 823.50 level.
"The central bank intervened as the dollar's strength continued due to rising importer settlements," said a dealer with a domestic bank.
The BOK never says when it has stepped in.
The won rose to 822.10 after opening at 823.40. It moved between a high of 821.90 and a low of 823.60.
Dealers said trading would range from 821.00 to 823.50 this afternoon with many banks staying on the sidelines on fears of further intervention.
